prerequisites: Mathematical Analysis I (differential and integral calculus for functions of one variable, numerical successions and series)

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus for functions of several real variables with real and vector values.
Presentation of the main methodological tools for the study of differential equations.
Knowledge and understanding of differential calculus in several variables for functions to real values.
Knowledge and understanding of integral calculus in several variables for real-valued functions.
Knowledge and understanding of curves and surfaces in the space.
Knowledge and understanding of conservative vector fields.
Knowledge and understanding of linear ordinary differential equations and separable variable differential equations.
Ability to analyze and solve problems related to the study of functions of several real variables.
Ability to analyze and solve problems related to the integral calculation of functions of several real variables.
Ability to calculate the length of a curve and the area of a surface.
Ability to recognize a conservative vector field and compute its potential.
Ability to solve problems through the use of differential equations.

syllabus_topics: Curves and their lengths, curvilinear integrals
Limits and continuity in several variables
Spherical neighborhoods. Open and closed sets. Weierstrass theorem
Partial and directional derivatives, differentiable functions, tangent plane. Gradient formula
Surfaces and their areas. Divergence theorem
Ordinary linear differential equations and differential equations with separable variables
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The written test, lasting 120 minutes, has four equally weighted exercises and must be passed to access the oral exam. A passed written test is valid throughout the exam session (January-February or June-September) and the oral test must be taken in the same session. The oral test, lasting 40 minutes, generally involves three theoretical questions. The final grade is a weighted average of the written test (1/3) and the oral test (2/3). Two intermediate written tests can be taken to be exempted from the final written exam, with their arithmetic mean becoming the written grade, provided the oral exam is taken in the summer session.
bibliography: M. Bramanti, C.D. Pagani, S.Salsa, Analisi Matematica 2, Zanichelli, 2009
